recipes.name: Cherry Cream Cheese Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (21 ounce) can light cherry pie filling

steps.text: Beat cream cheese until light and fluffy. Gradually stir in sweetened condensed milk and continue mixing until smooth and combined. Add lemon juice and vanilla; mix well.
Pour filling into graham cracker crust. Refrigerate until set, 2 to 4 hours.
Just before serving, spread cherry pie filling over the top.

raw_recipe.headline: Cherry Cream Cheese Pie
raw_recipe.description: This cherry cream cheese pie is always a hit at parties and potlucks. It is an irresistible dessert that is easy to make but looks fancy.

review.reviewBody: Wow does this bring back memories...my Grandma Helen used to make this all the time and everyone loved it! She used to call it "Cherry O'Cream Cheese Pie". This was very easy to make and very good and while it's not a "cheesecake" it's not bad for so few ingredients and being "no bake". I followed the recipe exactly but I did change up the graham cracker crust this time. I used a chocolate version to give it a "black forest" flavor. Definitely chill it for at least 3 hours and don't overbeat your ingredients for those who found it didn't firm up. I'm sure then it'll come out just like hers did. And like Grandma's always do, she'd add whipped cream on top! Those were the days...

I put these in fridge over night but found they were not set up the way I would like maybe I over beat the cream cheese mix. My solution was to put in a preheated 350° oven for 8 minutes and it was close to perfect at this point and would give it a 5 star rating. I will make these again soon and update my review but if you plan on a no bake recipe and you have to bake them I think 3 stars is fair if it was my error from over mixing this recipe is a solid 5 star. I made some fresh whipped cream to pipe on these they where gone at our bbq joint in 1 1/2 hours! Blueberry is next!

One of our family favorites! I don't typically use the almond extract though. I used to make as a pie with the graham cracker crust, but have recently started making these as dessert cups with mini nilla wafers as the "crust" in the bottom, then just spoon filling on top. To do 8 6-oz servings, you need to double this recipe. For those complaining about the cherries sinking or the filling not setting, I wait until just before serving to put the cherries on.

My mom used to make this when I was a kid, so I was thrilled to stumble across this recipe. I find 1/3cup of lemon juice to be too much, so I cut it back to 1/4cup. If I don't have a graham cracker crust in the house, I simply put the cream cheese in casserole dish, then top it with the cherry filling. Super easy and delicious. I'm guessing those that are having problems with the consistency are using evaporated milk instead of condensed. BIG difference.

This is the Eagle Brand Cherry Cheese Pie recipe, I’ve made this hundreds of times and it has never failed. Its super sweet and has a soft filling but should not be soupy. I think the reviewers who had problems may have used the tub of cream cheese-which is actually a spread with a softening ingredient. Only use the block of cream cheese, and also wait to add the topping until it has set. Oh, and use a mixer on the cream cheese before adding any other ingredients or you’ll get lumps.

For Firmer Pie: Try Knox (unflavored) Gelatin. Into 1/3 cup of fresh squeezed lemon juice, mix in 1 1/2 to 2 tsp & let it stand for 1 minute (lemon juice will 'swell' or thicken). Incorporate into cream cheese/milk mixture. If you use fresh--crush your pulp or strain it. Do not use too much of the Knox or your pie will be more gelatinous than the creamy texture this delicious pie is known for. Using the Knox means you don't have to sacrifice your lemony flavor by cutting it due to 'soupy' problems and you do not have to add extra cream cheese either which to me, cuts into the other flavors. Try not putting all that 'cherry glop' (sorry, I hate tha stuff) on the whole pie but spoon over individual slices. This will keep pie filling from 'saggin' because of the heavy weight of filling. It also keeps pie from leaking after a few days (if it last that long) making the pie look 'unappealing'. I have never had a problem with soupy-ness or a pie that doesn't set at all. The Original recipe itself just yields a pretty soft texture. However, I experimented years ago with unflavored gelatin because I like my pies to cut 'clean'. This will do just that for you. And because it is unflavored...you don't interupt the original taste of the recipe. Call it an 'invisible band-aid'. I use sweetened thawed strawberries or frozen cherries mixed with sugar. I lost the recipe & knew someone would have it here. Thanks for posting.

Like so many others have stated, I've had trouble with this in the past due to the cream cheese collapsing (even after 6 hrs., or more, time to set). THIS time I added 1tsp of plain gelatin. What a difference! The pie is firm, even after slices have been taken from the pan. Can't wait to make it again!

After reading the other reviews I was worried about it being too sweet and not setting and the topping sinking. I added two eggs to the filing and baked at 350 for 35 minutes in a a water bath. Looked like a professional cheese cake. I refrigerated the pie overnight and added the topping several hours before dinner and continued chilling it in the refrigerator. To give it a black Forrest look I used a prepared Oreo crust and strawberry pie topping. Yum yum!

TLDR: loved it!

Deets: Philadelphia cream cheese original, not light. Harris-Teeter sweetened condensed milk. Honey Maid crust. Natural vanilla, fresh squeezed lemon juice.

I made sure the cream cheese was properly softened so it would blend right. ("Softened" means room temperature, BTW.) 

I was worried about the excessive lemon flavor noted in some reviews, so used 1/4 cup. The lemon was completely unnoticeable except when I was looking for it. The full 1/3 cup would have been fine.

It set perfectly in the fridge overnight.

We added lemon slices as a garnish.

This is a fabulous pie. Will definitely make again.
It DOES take 2 8oz. blocks of cream cheese, not 1. Fix the recipe!

This is the first 'pie' I made as a teenager in 1974 using bottled lemon juice!Please use Sweetened Condensed milk NOT evaporated milk. Also, stir juice, vanilla and zest (if using) into smoothly beaten cream cheese/milk mixture. Let set up in fridge 2-3 hours THEN top with pie filling or spoon filling on slices after plating to keep filling from sinking into pie. Easy, refreshing dessert.

I have been making this recipe for 45 years. I even have the original paper label that came off the can with the recipe on it. It’s a wonderful recipe. It has a sweet and tangy taste between the lemon juice and the sweeten condensed milk. You can use any type of pie filling from a can just use what you like or use no topping, we eat it that way most of the time.
I only use 1/4 cup lemon juice and it sets better to my preferences.
So easy and delicious and none left from the dinner we brought it to at church. Definitely will stay on the dessert rotation.
Absolutely a game changer. Been a family favorite for years.
does not set up waste of money

If you are looking for a quick, sweet treat, this is not it. I previously made one similar to this and was looking for the recipe when I came across this one. It looked close so I made it. I followed exactly but this is gross. It has far too much vanilla and didn't set at all. It went in the trash. I should have paid closer attention to"modified the original and..."
Runny. I followed the directions exactly and it never set up. Going back to my old recipe. Very disappointed.
I make this every year for my daughter's birthday!
I was sure following all of the recommendations mine would set up. It did not. I put it in the freezer hoping it will firm up.
